name: Zabad
overview: Zabad was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, identified specifically as a son of Ephraim. His life is noted in Scripture for his death at the hands of the men of Gath, marking a violent episode in his history. This brief mention situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribal history and conflicts.
namesAndTitles: The name Zabad means 'he bestows,' a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:21. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it reflects a common Hebrew personal name of the time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Zabad as a son of Ephraim, connecting him to the prominent tribal ancestor. It is also inferred that Shuthelah was his father, placing Zabad within a known genealogical line in the tribe of Ephraim. No other family relationships are recorded beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Zabad's significance lies in his tribal identity and his death at the hands of the men of Gath, which reflects the ongoing struggles and hostilities between Israelite tribes and neighboring peoples. His mention in the genealogical record underscores the importance of lineage in God's providential plan for Israel. Though his role is brief, it contributes to the historical and spiritual tapestry of the nation of Israel as preserved in Scripture.
